We work in this folder: raw, references, done. Install and verify 5 tools: FFmpeg with libass (on Mac: ffmpeg-full, full path), faster-whisper for word-level subtitles, yt-dlp for references, Remotion, HyperFrames (npm package hyperframes). Check what's installed first. Official installs only (Homebrew, winget, npm/pip), Node.js 22+. Python packages go in a .venv here: pip install faster-whisper "av<19". Study each one frame by frame and by ear: pacing, shot length, pause cuts, subtitles, colors, graphics, transitions, music, the first 3 seconds. Take inspiration, but don't copy: no shots, text, logos or brand elements. Write my own style to style.md with exact values. Show it to me. PROMPT 3: EDIT My new recording is in raw. Edit it using style.md: 1. Transcribe with Whisper, word timestamps. Ask me about doubtful words before burning subtitles. 2. Cut pauses, slips and bad takes, keep the last good take. Keep pauses that serve the meaning. Don't speed up my voice. 3. Word-by-word subtitles in my style. 4. If references/music.mp3 exists, put it quietly under the voice. 5. Graphics only where they help. 6. Export 1080x1920 to done as draft-v1.mp4 plus edit-notes.md. Check the file, then show me. Save my fixes as draft-v2, draft-v3. How Cloudflare's Code Mode Supercharges MCP! 🤖⚡ Despite claims that Cloudflare's Code Mode replaces the Model Context Protocol (MCP), it actually makes MCP dramatically more efficient. In a traditional setup, an AI agent loads thousands of tokens of tool descriptions upfront and executes actions one round trip at a time. Asking a model to schedule 31 distinct calendar events forces 31 separate inference loops, re-sending the entire conversation history and tool schemas on every single step. Code Mode eliminates this bottleneck by automatically converting MCP tool definitions into standard programming functions, allowing the model to write one short script with a loop instead of making dozens of individual tool calls. That generated script runs inside an isolated sandbox with no open internet access, communicating exclusively with the underlying MCP server under the agent's existing permissions. The program handles all 31 API calls locally and returns a brief summary to the model, slashing token usage by 81 percent. This pattern also solves massive context bloat at enterprise scale. Rather than stuffing over a million tokens of schemas for 2,500 platform actions into a prompt, Cloudflare's own MCP server exposes just two tools, one to search for actions and one to execute code, shrinking the footprint to roughly a thousand tokens. #ModelContextProtocol #Cloudflare #AIAgents #SoftwareEngineering #SystemDesign #TechExplained

Claude Code just got an experimental Code Mode, and it changes how Claude works. Normally it goes one step at a time: run a command, read the result, think, repeat. Every one of those results lands in your context. With Code Mode on, Claude writes a single script that makes those tool calls in one go. It runs them in parallel and only keeps the part of the output it actually needs. It's off by default. To turn it on, paste this into Claude Code: "Turn on Code Mode for me. Check that claude --version is 2.1.323 or later and run claude update if it isn't. Then add CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE set to "1" in the env block of ~/.claude/settings.json, keeping everything else in the file as it is. Tell me when it's done so I can restart Claude Code in a terminal." Want to master Claude Code, even with zero experience? Or learn to edit videos like this one with Claude?
